name: manual_ecf446
claim: When a script compares 'sibling repositories' by directory path, a linked git worktree of the SAME canonical repo is not a downstream mirror target — it's an alternate checkout of the identical guard authority. Distinguish them via 'git -C <root> rev-parse --git-common-dir' (resolved to an absolute path): if two roots share the same common dir, they're worktrees of one repo, not independent siblings, and should be skipped rather than scanned for divergence.

decisions.notes: Found by another agent (Codex) reviewing PR 311's merged fix: linked orama-system worktrees (used throughout this same session for parallel PR work) were being scanned as if they were independent downstream repos, producing false-positive divergence failures against pre-merge worktree state. Fixed in orama-system PR 312, synced to PT as commit 0f9472f6. The git-common-dir comparison is the correct primitive -- 'git worktree list' parsing or path-prefix heuristics would be more fragile.
